plugins.readme:
# Classic Themes

Classic Dark and Classic Light for Flux: calm color schemes — warm gray and white — on Flux's frosted
glass. The two themes are a pair: choose them as the dark and the light theme of **Settings →
Appearance → Theme → Sync with OS**, and Flux follows macOS between them.

- **Classic Dark** — warm gray neutrals. Code: keywords, commas and semicolons orange, strings green,
  numbers blue, functions yellow, fields and constants purple (constants in italics), annotations
  olive, doc comments green italic.
- **Classic Light** — white islands on pale gray. Code: keywords dark blue, strings green, numbers
  blue, function declarations teal, fields and constants purple, annotations olive, comments gray
  italic.
- In both, plain identifiers and types keep the text color; selection, focus, changed files and diffs
  use the scheme's own colors, and the terminal has a matching ANSI table.

Version 0.2 gave the themes these names: a Flux that had one of them chosen under its former name
keeps it.

ru.Classic Dark and Classic Light: calm col: Classic Dark и Classic Light — спокойные цветовые схемы, тёплая серая и белая, на матовом стекле Flux. Тёмная и светлая тема — пара для синхронизации с ОС.

# CSS

CSS and SCSS: highlighting, and the CSS language server with errors, completion, color and hover information, and formatting.

## Files

- **CSS**: `*.css`.
- **SCSS**: `*.scss`.

## Language servers

Flux starts the server when a file of the language opens. If it isn't on the machine, Flux
installs it into `~/Library/Application Support/flux/servers` (Settings → Language Servers shows
where each one comes from, and installs, updates or removes it).

- **vscode-css-language-server** (the npm package `vscode-langservers-extracted`) — with a Node.js of Flux's own; for CSS and SCSS.

## Highlighting

- [tree-sitter-css](https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-css) v0.25.0, MIT — the grammar and its highlighting query, adapted to Flux's theme scopes (`licenses/`).
- [tree-sitter-scss](https://github.com/savetheclocktower/tree-sitter-scss) `f5dfc3b`, MIT — the grammar and its highlighting query, adapted to Flux's theme scopes (`licenses/`).
- Less isn't here yet: there is no maintained tree-sitter grammar for it.

plugins.readme:
# Flux Tiles

File icons as colored tiles: each kind of file gets Flux's own glyph in white (near-black where
white wouldn't read) on a rounded tile of its color — Rust orange, TypeScript blue, Python blue
with a yellow snake, Go cyan, Docker blue, licenses gold. The tiles are full-color, so they look the
same on light and dark themes.

The set knows the same files as Flux Icons, the set Flux comes with. Folders keep Flux's own icons;
a file the set doesn't know gets a gray tile, unless its language plugin brings an icon of its own.

Choose it in **Settings → Appearance → File Icons**.

The icons are generated: `python3 src/gen-tiles.py <flux>/plugins/icons` reads Flux Icons and writes
`icons/` and `icon-themes/tiles.toml` (edit the script, not the generated files).

# Python

Python: highlighting, Pyright (types, completion, navigation, the project's virtual environment) and Ruff (linting and formatting).

## Files

- **Python**: `*.py`, `*.pyi`, `*.pyw`.

## Language servers

Flux starts the server when a file of the language opens. If it isn't on the machine, Flux
installs it into `~/Library/Application Support/flux/servers` (Settings → Language Servers shows
where each one comes from, and installs, updates or removes it).

- **Pyright** — from npm, with a Node.js of Flux's own. It uses the project's virtual environment (`.venv`, `venv` or `env` with a `pyvenv.cfg`, otherwise `$VIRTUAL_ENV`).
- **Ruff** — the latest release from GitHub (checked by its `.sha256`): linting and formatting (⌥⌘L).

## Highlighting

- The grammar and its highlighting query: [tree-sitter-python](https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-python) v0.25.0, MIT — `licenses/`.

# Solarized

Solarized Light and Solarized Dark for Flux: Ethan Schoonover's palette of sixteen colors with
fixed lightness relationships, on Flux's frosted glass. The two themes are a pair: choose them as
the light and the dark theme of **Settings → Appearance → Theme → Sync with OS**, and Flux follows
macOS between them.

- Code: keywords green, functions blue, types yellow, strings cyan, numbers magenta, comments in
  the quiet base tone.
- The terminal uses the classic Solarized ANSI table.

The palette is © Ethan Schoonover, MIT licence (`licenses/LICENSE-solarized`).

plugins.name: Yandex Tracker & Calendar
plugins.description: Yandex Tracker and Calendar in Flux: the board of tasks, a task with its links, comments and history, your own Claude actions on a task — Take to Work moves it, makes its branch, opens its tabs and hands Claude your prompt at once; links to tasks in code, commits and Claude's chat; the next meeting in the status bar with a reminder and Join.
plugins.manifest:
# Yandex Tracker and Calendar for Flux: the board of tasks in an editor tab, a task's card with its
# links, comments and history, your own Claude actions on a task (the favorite one — Take to Work on
# the board), tasks as Tasks & Contexts in JetBrains IDEs, and the day's meetings in the status bar. Sign-in — Yandex ID (OAuth with PKCE through the browser), the token
# in the keychain; the organization — Yandex 360 or Yandex Cloud.
id = "flux.yandex"
name = "Yandex Tracker & Calendar"
version = "0.1.0"
api = "0.3"
authors = ["Egor Ageev"]
description = "Yandex Tracker and Calendar in Flux: the board of tasks, a task with its links, comments and history, your own Claude actions on a task — Take to Work moves it, makes its branch, opens its tabs and hands Claude your prompt at once; links to tasks in code, commits and Claude's chat; the next meeting in the status bar with a reminder and Join."
repository = "https://github.com/egor4geev/flux-plugins"
icon = "icons/yandex.svg"
wasm = "target/wasm32-wasip2/release/flux_yandex.wasm"

[permissions]
# Git branches, the commit message template, the tabs of a task (contexts).
project = "write"
network = ["oauth.yandex.ru", "login.yandex.ru", "api.tracker.yandex.net", "caldav.yandex.ru"]
# The sign-in: Yandex ID returns to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback.
server = true
# Discuss and Plan with Claude: a session with the task.
claude = true

# Sign-in.
[[commands]]
id = "sign-in"
title = "Sign In to Yandex…"
category = "Yandex"

[[commands]]
id = "sign-out"
title = "Sign Out of Yandex"
category = "Yandex"

[[commands]]
id = "check-connection"
title = "Check Yandex Connection"
category = "Yandex"

# Tracker: the keys of JetBrains Tasks & Contexts.
[[commands]]
id = "open-task"
title = "Open Task…"
category = "Tracker"
keys = "alt-shift-n"

[[commands]]
id = "close-task"
title = "Close Active Task…"
category = "Tracker"

[[commands]]
id = "show-task"
title = "Show Active Task"
category = "Tracker"

[[commands]]
id = "open-in-browser"
title = "Open Task in Browser"
category = "Tracker"
keys = "alt-shift-b"

[[commands]]
id = "log-time"
title = "Log Time…"
category = "Tracker"

[[commands]]
id = "toggle-timer"
title = "Pause or Resume Task Timer"
category = "Tracker"

[[commands]]
id = "discuss-task"
title = "Discuss Task with Claude"
category = "Tracker"

[[commands]]
id = "open-board"
title = "Open Task Board"
category = "Tracker"

[[commands]]
id = "refresh-tasks"
title = "Refresh Tasks"
category = "Tracker"

# The active task's status bar item: its menu.
[[commands]]
id = "task-menu"
title = "Active Task Menu"
category = "Tracker"
palette = false

# A notification's Open: the task in the window (`argument` — its key).
[[commands]]
id = "open-notified-task"
title = "Open Task"
category = "Tracker"
palette = false

# Calendar.
[[commands]]
id = "calendar-agenda"
title = "Show Today's Meetings"
category = "Calendar"

[[commands]]
id = "calendar-join"
title = "Join Meeting"
category = "Calendar"

[[commands]]
id = "calendar-refresh"
title = "Refresh Calendar"
category = "Calendar"

[[tool-windows]]
id = "tracker"
title = "Tracker"
icon = "icons/tracker.svg"

# The board: wide, among the editor's tabs; a card chosen on it opens in the Tracker window.
[[tool-windows]]
id = "board"
title = "Board"
icon = "icons/board.svg"
location = "editor"

[[status-items]]
id = "active-task"

[[status-items]]
id = "next-meeting"

# Settings → the plugin: all about the account and the organization.

[[settings]]
key = "account"
type = "section"
title = "Account"
description = "Sign in with your Yandex ID — or paste a token below instead."

[[settings]]
key = "account-status"
type = "status"
title = "Account"
default = "Not signed in"

[[settings]]
key = "sign-in-button"
type = "button"
title = "Sign In with Yandex…"
command = "sign-in"

[[settings]]
key = "sign-out-button"
type = "button"
title = "Sign Out"
command = "sign-out"

[[settings]]
key = "oauth-token"
type = "secret"
title = "OAuth token"
description = "Instead of signing in: a Yandex OAuth token with tracker:read, tracker:write and calendar:all."

[[settings]]
key = "iam-token"
type = "secret"
title = "IAM token"
description = "For a federated account of Yandex Cloud: `yc iam create-token` (it lives 12 hours)."

[[settings]]
key = "organization"
type = "section"
title = "Organization"
description = "Tracker → Administration → Organizations shows the ID."

[[settings]]
key = "org-id"
type = "string"
title = "Organization ID"

[[settings]]
key = "org-type"
type = "choice"
title = "Organization type"
default = "auto"
options = [
    { value = "auto", title = "By the ID: only digits — Yandex 360" },
    { value = "360", title = "Yandex 360" },
    { value = "cloud", title = "Yandex Cloud" },
]

[[settings]]
key = "check-connection-button"
type = "button"
title = "Check Connection"
command = "check-connection"

[[settings]]
key = "connection-status"
type = "status"
title = "Connection"

[[settings]]
key = "claude"
type = "section"
title = "Claude actions"
description = "Buttons of a task's card; the board shows the one marked On the board. A prompt takes the task's {key}, {summary}, {description}, {url}, {status}, {type}, {priority}, {assignee}, {author}, {queue}, {deadline}, {sprint}, {parent}, {branch}, {links}, {comments}."

[[settings]]
key = "actions"
type = "records"
title = "Actions"

[[settings.fields]]
key = "name"
title = "Name"
type = "string"

[[settings.fields]]
key = "prompt"
title = "Prompt"
type = "text"

[[settings.fields]]
key = "mode"
title = "Claude's mode"
type = "choice"
default = "default"
options = [
    { value = "default", title = "As in Claude's settings" },
    { value = "plan", title = "Plan mode" },
]

[[settings.fields]]
key = "start"
title = "Take the task to work first"
type = "bool"

[[settings.fields]]
key = "favorite"
title = "On the board"
type = "bool"

[[settings.default]]
name = "Take to Work"
mode = "default"
start = true
favorite = true
prompt = """
Take Yandex Tracker task {key} "{summary}" to work: {url}

{description}

Links:
{links}

Comments:
{comments}

Study the code it concerns, then implement the task. Answer in the task's language."""

[[settings.default]]
name = "Plan"
mode = "plan"
start = false
favorite = false
prompt = """
Study Yandex Tracker task {key} "{summary}" ({url}) and the code it concerns, then propose a plan; don't change anything yet.

{description}

Links:
{links}

Comments:
{comments}"""

[[settings]]
key = "work"
type = "section"
title = "Take to work"
description = "What an action that takes a task to work does before Claude gets the prompt."

[[settings]]
key = "work-status"
type = "bool"
title = "Move the task to In Progress"
default = true

[[settings]]
key = "work-branch"
type = "bool"
title = "Create or check out the task's branch"
default = true

[[settings]]
key = "work-context"
type = "bool"
title = "Switch to the task's tabs"
default = true

[[settings]]
key = "work-timer"
type = "bool"
title = "Start the task's timer"
default = true

[[settings]]
key = "offer-worklog"
type = "bool"
title = "When a task is closed, offer to log its time"
default = true

[[settings]]
key = "tracker"
type = "section"
title = "Tracker"
description = "Your list of tasks, a task's branch and its commit message."

[[settings]]
key = "my-query"
type = "string"
title = "My tasks"
description = "What the Tracker window lists as My Tasks: a query in Tracker's language."

[[settings]]
key = "branch-template"

[[settings]]

[[settings]]

title = "Notifications"

[[settings]]
key = "poll-minutes"
type = "integer"
title = "Check for news every (minutes)"
default = 2
min = 1
max = 60

[[settings]]
key = "notify-assigned"
type = "bool"
title = "Tasks assigned to me"
default = true

[[settings]]
key = "notify-summoned"
type = "bool"
title = "When I'm summoned"
default = true

[[settings]]
key = "notify-status"
type = "bool"
title = "Status changes of my tasks"
default = true

plugins.readme:
# Yandex Tracker & Calendar

Yandex Tracker and Yandex Calendar in Flux: your tasks on a board, work on a task with its branch and
its own tabs, and the day's meetings in the status bar.

## Signing in

**Settings → Plugins → Yandex Tracker & Calendar**:

- **Sign In with Yandex…** opens Yandex ID in the browser; after you allow access, the browser comes
  back to Flux on this Mac (`http://127.0.0.1:52580/callback`, or 52581, 52582 when it's busy) and the
  page says you're signed in. The token is kept in the macOS keychain.
- Instead: paste an **OAuth token** (with `tracker:read`, `tracker:write`, `calendar:all`), or an
  **IAM token** for a federated account of Yandex Cloud (`yc iam create-token`, it lives 12 hours).
- **Organization**: its ID (Tracker → Administration → Organizations) and its type — by the ID (only
  digits — Yandex 360), Yandex 360 or Yandex Cloud. **Check Connection** says who you are in Tracker.
- **Advanced → ClientID**: your organization's own Yandex ID app instead of Flux's (an app "for user
  authorization" with the three redirect addresses above).

## Tasks

The **Tracker** window on the right (its icon in the launchpad):

- **The list**: My Tasks (the query of the settings), Following, a queue's open tasks or a query of
  your own — the menu at the top; tasks grouped by status.
- **The card** of a task (a double click, ↵, a link): the key and the title; the status — click it for
  its transitions; type, priority, assignee, deadline, sprint, the parent task — and after them every
  other field the task has, as Tracker's own page lists them: the system fields (start and end,
  estimates and time spent, versions, the QA engineer, the project, the epic…) in Tracker's order,
  then the queue's own fields, named as Tracker names them (**Fewer Fields** keeps only the main
  ones). Click a field with ▾ to change it: a person, a date, one value of a list, a line or a number.
  Then the description; **Links** grouped by relation (subtasks, blocks, depends on, relates…), each opens its card;
  **Comments** with a field for a new one (⌘↵ sends) and **History** — who changed what, from what to
  what.
- **A button per Claude action** of the settings. An action sends Claude its prompt with the task's
  data in it: `{key}`, `{summary}`, `{description}`, `{url}`, `{status}`, `{type}`, `{priority}`,
  `{assignee}`, `{author}`, `{queue}`, `{deadline}`, `{sprint}`, `{parent}`, `{branch}`, `{links}`,
  `{comments}`. An action marked **Take the task to work first** does it in one click, as **Take to
  work** in the settings says: moves the task to In Progress, checks out its branch (an existing one
  whose name starts with the key, or a new one by the branch template), switches to the task's tabs,
  starts its timer — then Claude gets the prompt. The action marked **On the board** is the board's
  button. Two come with the plugin: Take to Work and Plan (plan mode).
- **Discuss with Claude**: a new Claude session with the task attached; you write what to do.

**The task in work** is in the status bar — `TRACK-142 · 0:42` — with a timer counted while Flux
runs; its menu: Show, the actions, Log Time…, pause, Close…, Open in Browser. While a task is in work
the commit message starts with it (the commit template of the settings). **Close** logs the time (the
timer's, editable: `1h 25m`, `1ч 25м`, `85m`, `1.5h`), moves the task, switches back to the branch
and the tabs from before the task.

**Open Task** (⌥⇧N) finds a task by its key or words; **⌥⇧B** opens the task in the browser.

Task keys of your queues — `TRACK-142` — are links in the editor (⌘-click; a hover tells the title,
the status and the assignee), in commit messages and in Claude's chat; a click opens the card.

Every few minutes (the settings say how often) the plugin checks for news: tasks newly assigned to
you, status changes of your tasks, and tasks where you're summoned — a notification with Open.

## The board

**Tracker: Open Task Board** opens the board of tasks as a tab among the editor's tabs, as boards
are in Tracker: the board's columns side by side, each with the tasks in its statuses — the key
and the title, the type and the assignee, the priority unless it's the usual one; the task you're
working on is marked ▶. A task in a status no column takes goes to a last column, Other statuses,
rather than out of sight. A scrum board shows its current sprint; a board made of a filter (a queue,
tags) shows what the filter finds.

- **The board** — the menu in the toolbar lists your boards: your favorite boards first, then all
  the others by name. ☆ next to it makes the shown board a favorite. The tab opens the board you
  chose last — at first, your first favorite, or the most recently changed board.
- **Filters**, as on Tracker's boards: **Only mine**, then **Assignee**, **Type**, **Priority**,
  **Tags** and **Components** — each lists the values the board's tasks have, with how many tasks
  show if you choose it; choose one, then another (the menu stays open, Esc closes it): several values
  of one filter show any of them, the filters together narrow each other. The field in the toolbar
  filters by words of the key or the title. A column says how many of its tasks show — "2 of 5";
  × clears the filters. Each board keeps its filter until you change it.
- **Saved filters** — save the current filter of a board under a name and choose it later from the
  same menu (or delete it there).
- **Take to Work** — the favorite Claude action of the settings (the one marked On the board; its
  name is the button's) on the selected task: it moves the task, makes its branch, opens its tabs
  and hands Claude the prompt, as the settings say.
- A task opens in the Tracker window on the right with a double click or ↵.
- The board refreshes when its tab shows, every two minutes while it shows, and when a task on it
  changes in Flux; ⟳ refreshes it now, the globe opens it in Tracker.

## Calendar

Your Yandex Calendar meetings, without leaving the code:

- **The next meeting in the status bar** — "Daily in 12 min", "Daily now · 5 min left", "Review at
  15:00"; nothing when the rest of the day is free. The tooltip has its time, place and whether it
  is on Telemost.
- **The agenda** — click the meeting in the status bar (or **Calendar: Show Today's Meetings**) for
  today's and tomorrow's meetings; choose one to join its Telemost conference (or the link in its
  place or description), or to open the day in Yandex Calendar when it has none.
- **A reminder** a few minutes before a meeting (**Remind before a meeting**, 5 by default; 0 turns
  it off), with **Join**. All-day events are in the agenda, not reminded of.
- **Calendar: Join Meeting** — the meeting going on, or the next one within the hour.

Meetings you declined and cancelled ones are left out; recurring meetings, moved and cancelled
occurrences and time zones are read as the calendar has them. **Hidden calendars** (by name) keeps
a calendar out — say, a colleague's you subscribed to.

The calendar uses the sign-in's token. If your organization's admin doesn't allow it, or your
account is a federated one, make an app password for CalDAV in Yandex ID (Security → App passwords
→ Calendar) and put your `login@domain` and the password into **CalDAV login** and **App password
for CalDAV** — a new app password starts working in a couple of hours.
